newsitem.title: USA: Micron to use Iomega Zip drive in new notebook computer.
newsitem.headline: Micron to use Iomega Zip drive in new notebook computer.

text.p: Iomega Corp. said Monday its internal notebook Zip drive will be included as an optional feature in Micron Electronics Inc.'s new TransPort XKE notebook computers.

Designed as an internal Zip drive for original equipment manufacturers to build into laptop computers, the notebook Zip drive will use standard 100 megabyte Zip disks, which provide 70 times the capacity and higher performance than traditional floppy disk drives.

In addition to Micron, Iomega said it has OEM deals with Chicony Electronics Co. Ltd., VST Technologies, CNF Technologies, and NEC Computer Systems Division to provide notebook Zip drives. Micron's TransPort XKE is a top-of-line notebook computer and uses an Intel Pentium processor.
Iomega's notebook Zip drive is expected to be available to laptop computer makers in the second half of 1997.
Iomega, based in Roy, Utah, said more than 6 million Zip drives have been shipped.
Micron Electronics is majority owned by Micron Technology Inc., based in Boise, Idaho.
